trust_decision.summary: Whether a URI from untrusted content (terminal output, remote HTML, plugin metadata) may go to the OS protocol handler without a prompt. At the pinned commit nothing decides this: ElectronPlatformService.openExternal passes every scheme straight to shell.openExternal. The fix adds an http/https/ftp/mailto allowlist and a confirmation dialog for other schemes.

landing_point.why: The summary names the 'terminal linkifier'. URLHandler's regex accepts any 3-9 letter scheme (tabby-linkifier/src/handlers.ts:15) and passes the match to platform.openExternal. The OSC 8 linkHandler in tabby-linkifier/src/decorator.ts:23-29 is the second obvious place to look.

fix_sites.entry_point: PlatformService.openExternal (public plugin API). Callers: linkifier URL/IP/file handlers, OSC 8 linkHandler, fastHtmlBind anchors, plugin homepage, config-sync host
fix_sites.module_kind: lower-level platform service, Electron implementation (tabby-electron package)

fix_sites.entry_point: abstract PlatformService API signature only (void -> Promise<void>)
WebPlatformService.openExternal (web build). Signature change only; still window.open with no scheme check

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: tabby-electron/src/services/platform.service.ts:143-145 (the real fix lives in the Electron platform service, not in tabby-linkifier where the report leads)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could say the report is about the linkifier, so filtering schemes in URLHandler/decorator is enough, and that PlatformService.openExternal is a general API used by trusted, hard-coded URLs that should not change. That would leave the fastHtmlBind release-notes links (tabby-core/src/directives/fastHtmlBind.directive.ts:21) and the plugin homepage (tabby-plugin-manager/src/components/pluginsSettingsTab.component.ts:135) open.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: http/https/ftp/mailto links must still open with no prompt. Terminal file-path links (opened as file://) and IP links (opened as http://) must keep working. A fix that blocks every non-web scheme outright would break file-path links.

O6_input_shapes: scheme in mixed or upper case, normalised with toLowerCase (fix.diff:48)
leading/trailing whitespace around the URI, removed with trim before parsing (fix.diff:47)
unparseable URI: scheme is null, so the user is prompted instead of the link opening (fix.diff:38-41, fix.diff:49-50)
file:// from the file-path handler is not on the allowlist, so it now prompts (fix.diff:26 with tabby-linkifier/src/handlers.ts:53)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: UpdaterService.update calls electron.shell.openExternal directly, skipping the PlatformService check; the URL comes from the GitHub releases API html_url
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The URL comes from a fixed GitHub API endpoint over HTTPS, so an attacker does not control it in practice
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the fix (tabby-electron), different file

O8_uncovered_routes.route: WebPlatformService.openExternal still calls window.open(url) with no scheme check; the fix changed only its signature
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Web build: the browser applies its own external-protocol prompt, and the advisory concerns the desktop app

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a main-process IPC handler (e.g. 'app:open-external') that calls shell.openExternal on a renderer-supplied URL, used by a linkifier or menu path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The main process already imports shell and calls openExternal here; maintainers often route opening through IPC into the main process.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a file-path handler that opens through electron.shell.openPath / openExternal directly instead of PlatformService
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: BaseFileHandler already builds a file:// URL itself, and the sibling platform method openPath (tabby-electron/src/services/platform.service.ts:147-149) is right next to openExternal.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a markdown/HTML renderer that opens anchor hrefs through window.open or electron.shell instead of PlatformService
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Release notes are remote HTML (tabby-settings/src/components/releaseNotesTab.component.pug:12); a second renderer with its own click handler is a plausible maintainer change.

O9_family: unsafe external URI / protocol-handler invocation (CWE-184 incomplete scheme denylist; advisory tags CWE-601)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + yarn workspaces, webpack, Electron (native modules such as node-pty and windows-native-registry)
O10_build.project_tests: None found for tabby-linkifier, tabby-electron or tabby-core (no *.spec.ts). Hidden tests would have to unit-test ElectronPlatformService with a mocked ElectronService (shell, dialog).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Restrict the URLHandler regex or the decorator's openLink to http(s) inside tabby-linkifier, missing the OSC 8 linkHandler, fastHtmlBind and plugin-homepage callers, and breaking file-path links.

out_of_scope_notes: SFTP 'Edit locally' opens a remote-named downloaded file with the OS default app via shell.openPath (tabby-electron/src/sftpContextMenu.ts:41-49); different sink, not pursued.
unverified: Repo size in MB not measured.
present_in_latest is unknown for both O8 routes (no latest release supplied).
needs_gpu_kernel_gui flagged because the sink is Electron shell/dialog; unit tests with a mocked ElectronService look feasible but were not tried.

In practice the real fix is one function in one place (the signature changes are mechanical), and the O8 routes are weak (updater URL is not attacker-controlled; web uses browser prompts). By lessons-v2 this is close to single_site, which never produced a hard task; the flag was not set only because the O8 routes technically exist.

O1 counts attacker-influenced callers: OSC 8 linkHandler (tabby-linkifier/src/decorator.ts:24-28), URLHandler (tabby-linkifier/src/handlers.ts:24), fastHtmlBind release notes (tabby-core/src/directives/fastHtmlBind.directive.ts:21), plugin homepage (tabby-plugin-manager/src/components/pluginsSettingsTab.component.ts:135). How attacker-controlled the plugin homepage and release-notes data are was not checked in depth.
